safetyNote: Conditionally edible only after thorough cooking: raw or undercooked Amanita rubescens is hazardous because it contains a heat-labile haemolysin. It can be confused with the poisonous Amanita pantherina. Never decide whether to eat a wild mushroom from this plate alone.

sections.title: Cap and gills
sections.text: The cap starts rounded, then becomes convex to nearly flat, commonly about 5–15 cm across. Its colour varies widely from pale grey-pink to pinkish or reddish brown. Irregular flat grey, off-white or pink-grey veil fragments may remain on the surface, but rain can wash them away. The crowded gills are pale and may develop pink or rusty-red marks when handled.

sections.title: Stem, ring and base
sections.text: The whitish stem becomes pinkish to wine-red where bruised. A high, fragile, hanging ring has conspicuous fine grooves on its upper surface. The base is bulbous; remnants of the universal veil may form fragile flocculent patches or scales there, but there is no persistent membranous cup.

sections.title: Bruising, spores and habitat
sections.text: White flesh in the cap and stem slowly stains pink to dull wine-red when cut or bruised, particularly around damaged areas and the bulb. The spore deposit is white; the smooth microscopic spores are broadly ellipsoid and amyloid. It forms mycorrhizae with broad-leaved and coniferous trees and fruits on woodland soil, mainly from summer to autumn in temperate Europe.

sections.title: Confusion and cooking
sections.text: The reddish bruising, grooved ring and lack of a sac-like basal volva together help separate it from the poisonous panther cap, Amanita pantherina; no one feature is enough for safe identification. Swiss official mushroom-control guidance lists A. rubescens only with the instruction to peel the cap skin and cook it well because it contains a heat-labile haemolysin. The plate shows typical features, not every colour form.

traits: Very variable pale grey-pink to wine-brown cap with irregular flattened grey veil patches
Cap and stem flesh blush pink to wine-red after injury; gills may stain too
High, fragile hanging ring with grooves on its upper face
Bulbous base with fragile veil remnants, without a persistent membranous cup
Crowded pale gills and a white spore deposit
